searchAudit.objective: Explore Agentic Driving ideas at the causal boundary from language or visual reasoning to action, with emphasis on slow-thinking misses and timeouts, independently grounded repair, intermediate-representation action consequences, and selective reasoning budget under closed-loop safety constraints.
searchAudit.window: Primary emphasis on 2025-2026 Agentic Driving and current general CoT faithfulness, causal mediation, self-correction, and adaptive-compute work, with older foundational papers retained only where they define a direct baseline.

rulesApplied.primarySourcePolicy: Every retained reference resolves to an official paper record, proceedings page, OpenReview record, arXiv manuscript, or official project. Search snippets and local reports were lead sources, not substitutes for primary records.
rulesApplied.causalClaimPolicy: Observational rationale-action agreement is not called causal. Interventions must specify the changed mediator, held-fixed inputs, action consequence, negative controls, and independent unit.
rulesApplied.repairPolicy: A revised rationale is not a repair unless the action changes when needed and an evidence source independent of the repairing model verifies that the original violation was removed without introducing another violation.
rulesApplied.computePolicy: All routing candidates compare against compute-matched random, always-fast, always-slow, and simple confidence or complexity routers and account for deadline misses rather than average latency alone.

candidateHardStops.application: Text, visual-thought, tool, or representation corruption is treated as a test mechanism only. A candidate cannot claim a natural driving failure unless unmodified public model rollouts or released logs contain the failure.

Generic CoT faithfulness probes, activation patching, causal mediation, self-reflection, confidence routing, or safety projection do not survive unless they create a driving-specific estimand, decision mechanism, or falsifiable boundary not supplied by direct priors.
Repository existence is separated from a pinned commit, license, weights, data, dependencies, entry point, and a real run. Heavy CARLA paths do not satisfy the requested lightweight entry.

The executed AgentThink geometry smoke satisfies only a tool-level execution check. It is not evidence that AgentThink reasons faithfully, chooses the correct tool, or changes a driving action safely.
Each retained candidate states which architecture, router, repair interface, or evaluation practice would be rejected by a null or adverse result.

sourceAttempts.note: The review and specified local reports were read as scoped synthesis and lead generation. Claims were reopened on their official primary records before inclusion.
Used for current preprints and technical reports where no formal venue record was available.
ACL Anthology, CVF Open Access, PMLR, NeurIPS proceedings, and AAAI pages were preferred for formal publication records.
Used for ICLR publication status and current causal or adaptive-reasoning records.

Three official GitHub repositories were pinned to immutable commits. AgentThink exposed a bundled demo and a lightweight geometry function; full model paths remained blocked by weights, datasets, GPU, or simulator dependencies. Assets are recorded separately rather than double-counted as paper references.

limitations: VLADriveBench states that an architecture-agnostic toolkit is released, but no durable official repository URL was exposed on the arXiv record inspected in this pass; its CARLA experiments were therefore treated as paper evidence, not as a locally executable asset.
X-MIND, the 2026 cognitive dual-process paper, and the VLM/ViT dual-system preprint did not expose a verified public checkpoint-plus-lightweight evaluation chain in the primary records inspected.

The OpenDriveVLA repository and 0.5B release are public, but its documented evaluation requires nuScenes, UniAD caches, customized MMDetection3D components, DeepSpeed, and GPU execution; no task-level forward was claimed locally.
The AgentThink lightweight smoke used one bundled public demo coordinate and the pinned geometry function body. It did not load the 7B checkpoint, tool models, DriveLMM-o1 corpus, or action head.
No natural-frequency claim is made for reasoning corruptions. Candidate pilots must start from unmodified model failures and may use interventions only for identification or negative controls.

NAVSIM and nuScenes planning metrics are not treated as real-road closed-loop safety. They are acceptable for a two-week go/no-go only when the claimed estimand is restricted to paired action consequences in that evaluation regime.

verifiedReferences.title: VLADriveBench: Evaluating CoT-Action Relationship in VLA for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Combines observational CoT metrics with mid-pass CoT interventions and selfsplice controls; finds ORION can be observationally aligned yet epiphenomenal while Alpamayo v1.5 is more causally coupled.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for any generic CoT faithfulness or text-swap benchmark.

verifiedReferences.title: AgentThink: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Trains tool-augmented CoT and evaluates tool invocation plus reasoning on DriveLMM-o1, but does not identify downstream action mediation or closed-loop repair.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct baseline for tool-use candidates and the executed public demo asset.

verifiedReferences.title: X-Mind: Efficient Visual Chain-of-Thought via Predictive World Model for End-to-End Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Internalizes a compact predictive world model as visual CoT before action to avoid cascaded latency.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct prior for visual-thought and wrong-future amplification candidates.

verifiedReferences.title: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Routes visual inputs to fast meta-action or structured slow reasoning and reports routing F1, average latency, planning accuracy, and rule consistency.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct baseline for complexity routing; leaves deadline-conditioned action value and timeout regret open.

verifiedReferences.title: CogDriver: Integrating Cognitive Inertia for Temporally Coherent Planning in Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses temporally grounded narratives, sparse temporal memory, and spatiotemporal distillation to reduce planning jitter and improve Bench2Drive and nuScenes results.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for generic narrative-memory or cognitive-inertia candidates.

verifiedReferences.title: HybridDriveVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Visual CoT Reasoning and ToT Evaluation for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Predicts future visual scenes and evaluates waypoint sequences for safety, progress, and comfort.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct baseline for visual-CoT plus multi-trajectory deliberation.

verifiedReferences.title: From Representational Complementarity to Dual Systems: Synergizing VLM and Vision-Only Backbones for End-to-End Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Finds complementary VLM and ViT behaviors, proposes a scorer that selects between trajectories, and a fast-slow variant that invokes the VLM on 15 percent of scenes.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for confidence-only VLM/ViT routers; separate from the CVPR paper with the same HybridDriveVLA name.

verifiedReferences.title: DriveVLM: The Convergence of Autonomous Driving and Large Vision-Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Combines scene description, analysis, and hierarchical planning; DriveVLM-Dual pairs the VLM with a traditional stack and reports a production-vehicle prototype.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct hybrid-system baseline, without an isolated reasoning-to-action causal effect.

verifiedReferences.title: OpenDriveVLA: Towards End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Large Vision Language Action Model
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Provides an open VLA action model, public code, and a documented 0.5B checkpoint path for nuScenes open-loop evaluation.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Primary public action baseline and candidate pilot substrate, subject to heavy dependency setup.

verifiedReferences.title: Counterfactual VLA: Self-Reflective Vision-Language-Action Model with Adaptive Reasoning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Mines scenes where meta-actions bottleneck trajectories, invokes counterfactual reasoning selectively, and revises meta-actions before trajectory generation.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for generic self-reflection and adaptive reasoning; motivates an independent repair certificate rather than same-model revision.

verifiedReferences.title: Latent Chain-of-Thought World Modeling for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Represents possible action outcomes in a latent reasoning space and reports faster inference and trajectory gains over text-reasoning baselines.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct prior for latent thought as action-conditioned future modeling.

verifiedReferences.title: Unifying Language-Action Understanding and Generation for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: LinkVLA shares a language-action codebook, adds trajectory-to-caption understanding, and uses coarse-to-fine action generation.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for a plain language-action consistency loss or shared-token mechanism.

verifiedReferences.title: DriveVLA-W0: World Models Amplify Data Scaling Law in Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses future-image world modeling to densify supervision and a lightweight action expert for deployment latency.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Compute and world-model baseline; scaling gains do not identify the causal role of a thought representation.

verifiedReferences.title: ReasonBreak: Probing Vulnerabilities in Reasoning-Enabled Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Perturbs text while keeping open-loop vision fixed and also evaluates sampled corruptions in an interactive AlpaSim loop.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Shows a reasoning-channel action surface but does not identify natural occurrence or mediation.

verifiedReferences.title: What Do They See? Interpreting Complex Road Scenarios Through the Eyes of Vision-Language-Action Models for Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Vehicle Learning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: CVAA removes and inpaints objects, measures trajectory deviation, and traces representation changes through Alpamayo 1.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct prior for behavioral object interventions; its representation differences are not themselves causal responsibility.

verifiedReferences.title: GeoWorldAD: Geometry World Action Model for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Connects ego-aligned current geometry, future geometry, and iterative trajectory refinement.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct baseline for geometry-mediated action and wrong-future fallback.

verifiedReferences.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models What to See and Where to Look
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses driving-aware vision distillation and 2D trajectory-guided prompts to align visual attention with action-relevant regions.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for generic trajectory-guided attention mediation.

verifiedReferences.title: SimLingo: Vision-Only Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving with Language-Action Alignment
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Jointly trains closed-loop driving and language-action alignment tasks.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Strong direct baseline against generic language-action consistency training.

verifiedReferences.title: LMDrive: Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving with Large Language Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Establishes a language-conditioned closed-loop CARLA baseline.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Closed-loop comparator, but its CARLA stack is outside the lightweight execution requirement.

verifiedReferences.title: DriveGPT4-V2: Harnessing Large Language Model Capabilities for Enhanced Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Produces high-level decisions, waypoints, and controls in closed-loop simulation.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Strong language-enabled closed-loop action baseline.

verifiedReferences.title: ReCogDrive: A Reinforced Cognitive Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Reframes driving cognition away from slow autoregressive text and trains a reinforced cognitive planning framework.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct cognitive-driving baseline for explicit text versus action-oriented cognition.

verifiedReferences.title: VLR-Driver: Large Vision-Language-Reasoning Models for Embodied Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Introduces a vision-language-reasoning framework for embodied driving.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Recent direct reasoning baseline whose reported gains do not by themselves establish action mediation.

verifiedReferences.title: C-CoT: Counterfactual Chain-of-Thought with Vision-Language Models for Safe Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses a structured counterfactual action tree over critical objects, risk, alternative meta-actions, and final planning.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct collision for adding a generic counterfactual reasoning stage.

verifiedReferences.title: CausalVAD: De-confounding End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Causal Intervention
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Applies causal intervention to reduce confounding in end-to-end driving rather than layering an explanation module.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct causal-driving baseline and collision for generic causal-intervention transfer.

verifiedReferences.title: VLM-CASE: Vision-Language Model Enabled Context-Adaptive Safety Envelopes for Anticipatory Safe Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Maps VLM semantic context into physical and RSS-style safety envelopes.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Strong baseline for an independent action constraint; does not isolate or certify reasoning-attributable repair.

verifiedReferences.title: ORION: A Holistic End-to-End Autonomous Driving Framework by Vision-Language Instructed Action Generation
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Connects long-term context, language reasoning, and a generative planner in Bench2Drive.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Public-weight baseline and the epiphenomenal-CoT case in VLADriveBench.

verifiedReferences.title: CoT4AD: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Explicit Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Aligns perception, question, prediction, and action reasoning during training and uses implicit CoT at inference.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct baseline for explicit or implicit CoT alignment without causal consequence identification.

verifiedReferences.title: Lost in Fog: Sensor Perturbations Expose Reasoning Fragility in Driving VLAs
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Relates reasoning consistency under sensor perturbation to trajectory deviation and includes a matched CoC-generation ablation.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Robustness nearest neighbor; association and a mode ablation do not identify which reasoning content mediates safety.

verifiedReferences.title: VisualThink-VLA: Visual Intermediate Reasoning for Effective and Low-Latency Vision-Language-Action Policies
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses compact visual evidence tokens, selective routing, and counterfactual faithfulness tests for low-latency embodied action.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Cross-domain nearest neighbor that blocks a generic visual-evidence router or counterfactual token test.

verifiedReferences.title: DAST: Difficulty-Adaptive Slow-Thinking for Large Reasoning Models
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Adapts reasoning length to difficulty with a token-length budget and budget-aware preference optimization.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct general baseline for difficulty-adaptive slow thinking.

verifiedReferences.title: When to Continue Thinking: Adaptive Thinking Mode Switching for Efficient Reasoning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Learns when to continue reasoning and reports token reductions with small answer-accuracy loss.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct general baseline for adaptive continuation, but not deadline-censored control.

verifiedReferences.title: Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Shows complex strategies can lose to simple compute-matched baselines and that more compute can worsen Reflexion or debate.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Requires compute-matched baselines and blocks more-compute-only candidates.

verifiedReferences.title: Optimizing Anytime Reasoning via Budget Relative Policy Optimization
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Optimizes outputs across sampled reasoning budgets with dense rewards from truncated traces.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Strong anytime-compute baseline; still evaluates answer reward rather than control deadlines and safety consequence.

verifiedReferences.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Intervenes on CoT through mistakes, paraphrases, truncation, and filler controls and finds task- and model-dependent reliance.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Foundational direct baseline for generic CoT intervention.

verifiedReferences.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Shows hidden biasing cues can shift answers while remaining absent from generated explanations.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Foundational evidence that plausible explanations can be post hoc.

verifiedReferences.title: Making Reasoning Matter: Measuring and Improving Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses causal mediation analysis across twelve LMs and finds intermediate reasoning is not reliably used; FRODO trains a reasoning module to use counterfactual inferences.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Direct causal-mediation nearest neighbor.

verifiedReferences.title: Measuring Chain of Thought Faithfulness by Unlearning Reasoning Steps
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Defines parametric faithfulness by unlearning information in reasoning steps and measuring prediction changes.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Blocks a parameter-erasure or unlearning-only faithfulness contribution without driving action consequences.

verifiedReferences.title: Is Chain-of-Thought Really Not Explainability? Chain-of-Thought Can Be Faithful without Hint Verbalization
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Argues that non-verbalized hints may still be mediated through CoT and that omission should not be conflated with causal irrelevance.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Requires action candidates to distinguish incomplete narration from absent mediation.

verifiedReferences.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses the same model as generator, feedback provider, and refiner and reports broad task gains.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Strong baseline for same-model iterative refinement.

verifiedReferences.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Stores verbal reflections derived from task feedback and uses them in subsequent agent trials.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: External-feedback reflection baseline; feedback source must be separated from self-consistency.

verifiedReferences.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Finds intrinsic self-correction without external feedback can fail or degrade reasoning, with prompt-design caveats documented in review.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Blocks treating same-model reflection text as independent repair evidence.

verifiedReferences.title: Inducing Causal Structure for Interpretable Neural Networks
verifiedReferences.primaryEvidence: Uses interchange intervention training to align high-level causal variables with neural representations.
verifiedReferences.auditUse: Foundational activation/interchange baseline; a driving application must add a new action consequence or mechanism.

candidateLedger.title: Generic CoT-to-action faithfulness probe for driving VLAs
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Swap, truncate, or corrupt driving CoT and measure whether the trajectory changes.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: None without a new consequence estimand or action mechanism; selfsplice and semantic CoT interventions are already direct driving evidence.

candidateLedger.title: Activation patching of reasoning tokens into the trajectory expert
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Patch hidden states from one scene or rationale into another and attribute downstream trajectory changes to a reasoning circuit.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Activation or interchange intervention is a mature method, CVAA already traces silent and amplified pathways, and the requested scope explicitly disallows activation patching as the contribution.

candidateLedger.title: Swap future sketches or geometry latents and measure trajectory deviation
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Intervening on X-MIND-like sketches or GeoWorldAD-like future geometry reveals whether visual thought causes actions.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: A swap audit alone is a visual restatement of the generic faithfulness probe and lacks a safety-conditioned mechanism or admissible intervention contract.

candidateLedger.title: Ask the same driving VLA to critique and revise its own action
candidateLedger.coreClaim: An extra reflection prompt will repair unsafe trajectories.
nearestCollision: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Counterfactual VLA already trains selective self-reflection, and same-model agreement is not independent evidence of repair.

candidateLedger.title: Route visually complex scenes to slow reasoning
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A scene-complexity classifier can reduce average latency while preserving planning accuracy.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: The routing object and mean-latency trade-off are directly occupied; complexity does not estimate the action-level value of thinking or timeout harm.

candidateLedger.title: Invoke a VLM when a vision-only trajectory scorer is uncertain
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Confidence-threshold routing captures complementary VLM and ViT behavior efficiently.
nearestCollision: From Representational Complementarity to Dual Systems
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: DualDriveVLA already uses scorer confidence for a 15 percent VLM route; replacing the confidence estimator does not create a new scientific object.

candidateLedger.title: Increase CoT tokens, samples, or deliberation branches for hard scenes
candidateLedger.coreClaim: More inference compute improves long-tail driving actions.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Additional compute is explicitly prohibited as the contribution and may lose to compute-matched simple baselines.

candidateLedger.title: Train a language-action consistency or bidirectional reconstruction loss
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Forcing rationales and trajectories to agree makes actions more faithful and safe.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Shared codebooks, bidirectional trajectory descriptions, language-action alignment, and rule consistency are already occupied; consistency can still be jointly wrong.

candidateLedger.title: Ablate AgentThink tools and compare downstream driving actions
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Tool evidence causally improves trajectories rather than only reasoning answers.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: The action consequence is worth measuring, but the pinned AgentThink path exposes reasoning QA and a 7B/tool stack rather than a lightweight action head, so the candidate lacks a matched public execution chain.

candidateLedger.title: Persistent narrative memory to reduce driving-action jitter
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A temporally coherent reasoning memory stabilizes multi-step maneuvers.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: CogDriver directly contributes temporally grounded narrative data, sparse memory, coherence distillation, and closed-loop gains.

candidateLedger.title: Use projected trajectories to force visual attention onto action-relevant regions
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Trajectory-guided visual prompts make visual thought causally action-relevant.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: DriveTeach-VLA already supplies 2D trajectory-guided prompts and action-oriented vision distillation; attention alignment alone is not an action-consequence estimand.

candidateLedger.title: Sample multiple critiques from the same VLA and vote on a repaired action
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Self-consistency across critiques filters incorrect reflections.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Voting consumes more compute, shares model errors, and supplies no independent repair witness; compute-matched studies show such strategies can worsen with budget.

candidateLedger.title: Safety-Bounded Reasoning Influence for Causally Useful but Non-Dominating Driving Thought
candidateLedger.coreClaim: A driving VLA can preserve action-relevant reasoning while bounding only the reason-mediated action residual with an independent feasible-action envelope, reducing harmful causal coupling without reverting to epiphenomenal explanations.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: VLADriveBench diagnoses whether CoT changes action but does not define how much causal influence is beneficial or harmful. VLM-CASE constrains final actions but does not decompose visual-base and reasoning-mediated residuals. The new object is a safety-conditioned complier effect plus an architecture that bounds only the reasoning channel.

estimands: Reasoning-mediated action effect: the paired trajectory contrast under semantically controlled reasoning interventions with vision, state, seed, and action decoder held fixed.

Harmful mediation mass: the episode probability that a reasoning intervention changes action and the changed action exits an independently computed feasible-action set while the base visual action remains inside.

Safety-conditioned complier effect: the change in safety cost among episodes where reasoning changes the action, reported separately for beneficial and harmful direction rather than as one average displacement.
newEstimandOrMechanism.mechanism: Decompose action into a vision-state base action plus a reason-mediated residual. An independent dynamics, occupancy, and rule envelope projects or rejects only the residual; evidence-consistent residuals remain causal, while unsafe residuals are clipped or removed and logged. Paired semantic and null interventions train the gate to preserve useful influence and reject formatting artifacts.

candidateLedger.title: Deadline-Censored Value of Thought Routing for Closed-Loop Driving
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Slow reasoning should be triggered by its expected action-level safety benefit before a control deadline, not by scene complexity or confidence alone, with explicit fallback when a slow result is censored by timeout.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Driving routers classify complexity, disagreement, or scorer confidence and primarily report mean latency. General adaptive reasoning optimizes answer reward per token. The new object is the paired net safety value of computation under deadline censoring, decomposed into trigger-miss regret and timeout regret over closed-loop episodes.

estimands: Per-episode net value of slow thought: safety loss of the fast action minus safety loss of the slow action if it arrives before the action deadline, otherwise minus the safety loss of the deadline fallback, with measured wall-clock latency included.
Trigger-miss regret: excess episode safety loss from routing a scene fast when a timely slow action would have reduced loss.
Timeout regret: excess episode safety loss attributable to invoking slow thought that misses the deadline, separated from slow-policy quality.
newEstimandOrMechanism.mechanism: Estimate a distribution over paired fast-versus-slow action benefit and slow completion time from pre-decoding features. Invoke slow thought only when its conservative expected net value is positive before the current control deadline; keep the fast action ready and commit it or a minimal-risk fallback at deadline. Allocate a finite reasoning budget across an episode rather than independently over frames.

candidateLedger.title: Independently Certified Action Repair Instead of Same-Model Reflection
candidateLedger.coreClaim: Reflection counts as repair only when an independent checker issues a concrete pre-action violation certificate and verifies that the revised action clears that violation without introducing a new one.
candidateLedger.noveltyResidual: Counterfactual VLA and C-CoT let a model reconsider actions, while VLM-CASE constrains actions. None of these direct records define repair as an attributable transition from an independently certified natural failure to a verified non-failure with new-violation accounting and a held-out checker that the repair model cannot author or score.

estimands: Certified repair effect among natural base-policy failures: difference in original-violation clearance between certificate-grounded repair and same-model reflection on paired episodes.
New-violation introduction rate: probability that a repair clears the cited constraint but violates another independent constraint.
Repair necessity precision: fraction of invoked repairs where the initial action truly violates the held-out checker, preventing gains from indiscriminate replanning.
newEstimandOrMechanism.mechanism: A non-generative dynamics, occupancy, and traffic-rule checker emits a minimal certificate containing constraint ID, first violation time, and responsible state. The VLA may revise its action using the certificate but cannot generate or score it. The checker re-evaluates the revision; failed or newly unsafe repairs fall back to a documented base or minimal-risk action.

shortlist.title: Safety-Bounded Reasoning Influence for Causally Useful but Non-Dominating Driving Thought
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It does not ask only whether CoT affects action. It estimates when that causal influence helps or harms safety and introduces a channel-specific bound that can preserve useful reasoning while preventing the reasoning residual from overriding an independently feasible base action.

newEstimandAndMechanism.primaryEstimand: Episode-level harmful mediation mass under semantically valid reasoning interventions, with the base visual action and independent feasible-action envelope held fixed.
secondaryEstimands: beneficial versus harmful safety-conditioned complier effects
newEstimandAndMechanism.mechanism: Base visual action plus explicitly isolated reason-mediated residual; an independent action envelope bounds only the residual and records every projection or rejection.

independentUnit.unit: One physical driving scene or route episode with a fixed sensor clip, ego state, actor initialization, and random seed, paired across original, semantic-intervention, null-intervention, and guarded branches.
notIndependent: multiple interventions from the same scene
independentUnit.analysis: Aggregate intervention contrasts within scene first, then use scene-level paired bootstrap or route-blocked intervals. No token- or frame-level pseudo-replication.

strongBaselines: unaltered causally coupled VLA, including Alpamayo-style CoT-conditioned action where available
epiphenomenal or detached-CoT action head represented by ORION-style weak coupling
final-action safety projection without reasoning-residual decomposition
VLM-CASE-style context-adaptive safety envelope
LinkVLA or SimLingo language-action alignment without causal influence bounds
random magnitude-matched residual clipping and always-reject reasoning residual

twoWeekGoNoGo.days1To2: Freeze one public action model path, preferably OpenDriveVLA 0.5B for open-loop trajectory generation and ORION or a public Alpamayo path for an explicit reasoning channel. Verify checkpoint revisions, 32-100 public mini scenes, and deterministic action decoding. Stop if no accessible model exposes a controllable reason-to-action interface.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days3To5: Implement selfsplice, paraphrase/null, semantically opposite, and evidence-consistent interventions. Pre-register the independent occupancy, kinematics, and traffic-rule envelope and verify that intervention formatting alone does not move actions.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days6To9: Measure paired action effects, beneficial/harmful complier effects, and harmful mediation mass. Implement base-action plus reason-residual decomposition and the channel-specific envelope.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days10To12: Compare against detached CoT, unguarded coupling, final-action projection, and random magnitude-matched clipping under identical scenes and compute.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days13To14: Reopen all apparent gains, inspect intervention validity and natural unmodified failures, and decide go or no-go from the predeclared conditions.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: At least one public model exhibits both beneficial and harmful natural reasoning-mediated action changes; channel-specific bounding removes a repeatable share of harmful changes while preserving a nonzero share of beneficial changes and outperforms ordinary final-action projection on progress at matched safety.
noGoConditions: Selfsplice or null interventions produce material action changes, making the mediator interface invalid.
Reasoning is wholly epiphenomenal or only harmful, so a simpler detached head dominates.
A standard final-action shield matches safety and progress, leaving no value in isolating reasoning influence.
Effects occur only under unnatural injected text and not in unmodified model errors.
No public model exposes a controllable reasoning-to-action path within the first two days.

shortlist.positiveResultValue: Would turn CoT-action causality from an interpretability property into a deployable influence contract: reasoning may alter action only inside a separately justified safety envelope, preserving useful long-tail corrections without allowing an unbounded reasoning channel.
shortlist.negativeResultValue: Would decide between simpler architectures: detach CoT if it is epiphenomenal or harmful, or use an ordinary final-action shield if residual-specific control adds no progress or diagnostic value.
publicExecutionChain: OpenDriveVLA fixed commit 10e8095bc618d508cb70cca37b6956ac4db6e9f3 provides public action code and a documented 0.5B checkpoint path.
ORION fixed commit 657f3cf09b745d3972affb84d68f7e376140b221 provides a direct public reasoning-action baseline.
VLADriveBench supplies the required intervention and selfsplice baselines at paper level; its code release must be independently pinned before reuse.
The go/no-go can use open-loop trajectories plus deterministic occupancy and rule checks; full CARLA is optional and not required.
knownRisks: A clean base-action/reason-residual decomposition may not exist in monolithic autoregressive VLAs.
Semantic text interventions can be out of distribution; null and source-matched controls are mandatory.
The independent envelope may dominate the result and reduce the contribution to ordinary shielding.
Public checkpoints may not reproduce the intervention access used by VLADriveBench.

shortlist.title: Deadline-Censored Value of Thought Routing for Closed-Loop Driving
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It replaces scene difficulty with a decision-theoretic object that driving routers do not currently report: whether slow thought changes the action beneficially before the control deadline, including false-negative and timeout costs under a finite episode budget.

newEstimandAndMechanism.primaryEstimand: Episode-level net value of slow thought under measured completion time and a fixed action deadline, with timeout fallback included in the potential outcome.
secondaryEstimands: budget-normalized safety gain over a route
newEstimandAndMechanism.mechanism: A pre-decoding router jointly predicts paired fast/slow action benefit and slow completion-time distribution, invokes slow reasoning only when timely net safety value is positive, and keeps a fast or minimal-risk action ready at the deadline.

independentUnit.unit: One route episode with fixed initial state and random seed, replayed under all routing policies and reasoning budgets.
notIndependent: multiple budget levels from the same episode
multiple candidate trajectories from one decoding call
independentUnit.analysis: Compute per-episode safety, progress, trigger-miss, timeout, and cost contrasts, then block by route family and bootstrap episodes.

strongBaselines: always fast
always slow
random trigger matched on number of slow calls and total tokens
visual complexity Arbiter from Cognitive Dual-Process Planning
confidence scorer routing from DualDriveVLA
disagreement or high-value-scene trigger from Counterfactual VLA
DAST or adaptive continuation with the same token budget but no action deadline

twoWeekGoNoGo.days1To2: Create one-model fast/slow branches on a public action VLA: direct trajectory versus bounded reasoning before trajectory, at 0/32/64/128 reasoning tokens. Freeze wall-clock instrumentation and a per-scene action deadline derived from the control interval, not a tuned acceptance threshold.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days3To5: Run paired branches on 100-300 public mini scenes or cached trajectories, record action deltas, safety proxies, completion times, and natural unmodified failures. Fit no router yet.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days6To8: Estimate benefit and completion-time models using scene-disjoint folds. Add a deadline fallback that never waits past the action deadline.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days9To12: Compare all strong baselines at identical total slow calls, tokens, and hardware. Report 95th and 99th latency, trigger-miss regret, timeout regret, and route-level safety/progress.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days13To14: Test one held-out condition such as low visibility or traffic-sign scenes and decide go or no-go without retuning the deadline.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: Timely slow-thought benefit is heterogeneous and predictable out of scene; the value router reduces route-level safety loss or certified violations relative to complexity, confidence, random, always-fast, and always-slow policies at matched compute, without increasing timeout regret.
noGoConditions: Slow reasoning has no stable positive action consequence after compute matching.
Benefit cannot be predicted out of scene better than random or confidence routing.
Timeout fallback erases the apparent gain or tail latency exceeds the fixed control deadline too often.
Always-fast or always-slow lies on the same safety-cost frontier and dominates the learned router.
The result depends only on choosing a larger token budget rather than selective allocation.

shortlist.positiveResultValue: Would provide a deployable routing target and evaluation protocol that prices missed hazards and late reasoning directly in action safety, replacing average latency and generic difficulty labels.
shortlist.negativeResultValue: Would show that current slow-thinking branches do not have predictable timely action value, supporting a simpler fixed policy or an independent safety monitor instead of a learned cognitive router.
publicExecutionChain: OpenDriveVLA fixed commit 10e8095bc618d508cb70cca37b6956ac4db6e9f3 supplies a public small action model path for direct versus bounded-reasoning prompts after environment setup.
The cognitive dual-process, DualDriveVLA, and Counterfactual VLA records define direct router baselines even where their code is not yet pinned.
Open-loop trajectory generation plus deterministic timing and occupancy checks can decide the first go/no-go; no CARLA server is required.
knownRisks: A prompt-defined fast/slow pair may differ from a jointly trained dual-process model and must be framed as a pilot substrate, not the final architecture.
GPU timing noise can confound completion-time estimates; warm-up, fixed batching, and hardware logging are required.
Open-loop safety proxies may disagree with reactive closed-loop outcomes, so claims remain at the tested evaluation level.
Rare hazardous trigger misses may be underpowered in a mini split.

shortlist.title: Independently Certified Action Repair Instead of Same-Model Reflection
shortlist.whyItSurvives: It narrows reflection to an auditable state transition: an unmodified action first fails an independent checker, the checker provides a minimal certificate, and a revision counts only if the same independent unit clears the original violation without creating another. This is stricter than generating a more coherent rationale or a second action from the same model.

newEstimandAndMechanism.primaryEstimand: Certified repair effect among naturally occurring base-policy violations, comparing certificate-grounded repair with same-model reflection on paired episodes.
secondaryEstimands: fallback rate when repair cannot be certified
newEstimandAndMechanism.mechanism: An independent non-generative checker issues a minimal time-indexed constraint certificate. The VLA receives it as external evidence and proposes a revision; only the checker can accept the revision, otherwise the system falls back.

independentUnit.unit: One natural base-policy failure episode with its original sensor clip, initial trajectory, checker certificate, repair attempts, and fallback outcome.
notIndependent: multiple certificates from the same trajectory
independentUnit.analysis: Sample-split by scene or route before checker calibration and model prompting. Pair all repair methods within episode and aggregate to episode-level clearance, new-violation, and progress outcomes.

strongBaselines: initial action with no repair
same-model intrinsic reflection without external evidence
Counterfactual VLA-style self-reflection
C-CoT action-tree reasoning
checker-only trajectory projection or final-action shield
oracle certificate with the true violated constraint and direct optimizer repair
random or irrelevant certificate negative control

twoWeekGoNoGo.days1To2: Run an unmodified public action model on a public mini split and enumerate natural occupancy, kinematic, drivable-area, and traffic-rule violations. Do not inject failures. Stop if fewer than a minimally analyzable set of natural failures appears.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days3To5: Freeze a checker that is non-generative and blind to model rationales. Emit one minimal certificate per initial failure: constraint ID, first violation time, and responsible state evidence.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days6To8: Implement certificate-grounded repair, same-model reflection, irrelevant-certificate control, checker-only projection, and fallback using identical action budgets.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days9To11: Measure original-violation clearance, new violations, progress, and unnecessary repairs in scene-disjoint folds. Manually reopen every apparent certificate-grounded success in the mini set.
twoWeekGoNoGo.days12To14: Run a held-out checker variant or route family to test whether the repair learned the certificate semantics rather than the checker's surface form, then decide go or no-go.
twoWeekGoNoGo.goCondition: On naturally occurring base-policy failures, certificate-grounded repair clears more original violations than intrinsic or Counterfactual-VLA-style reflection, introduces fewer new violations than free replanning, and retains more progress than checker-only projection or fallback.
noGoConditions: The public mini split has too few natural failures and only injected failures produce a result.
The checker-only projection dominates certificate-grounded repair on both safety and progress.
Irrelevant certificates perform as well as correct certificates, indicating generic replanning rather than evidence use.
Repairs frequently exchange one violation for another or fail under a held-out checker form.
The repair model can infer or influence checker acceptance, violating source independence.

shortlist.positiveResultValue: Would define a testable repair interface for Agentic Driving: reflection is accepted only with an external, machine-checkable action consequence, enabling regression tests and explicit fallback.
shortlist.negativeResultValue: Would reject language-mediated repair for the tested failure class and favor direct optimization, shielding, or immediate fallback, while also quantifying when same-model reflection is merely coherent self-justification.
publicExecutionChain: OpenDriveVLA fixed commit 10e8095bc618d508cb70cca37b6956ac4db6e9f3 provides public trajectory outputs after data setup.
Its evaluation code includes deterministic L2 and occupancy-collision machinery that can be adapted into a frozen checker without CARLA.
Counterfactual VLA, C-CoT, and VLM-CASE provide the direct reflection, counterfactual, and safety-envelope baselines at paper level.
knownRisks: Checker errors can create false certificates; all claims are conditional on the frozen checker and require manual audit on the mini set.
A certificate may reveal the optimal correction so directly that the contribution collapses to trajectory projection.
Natural failure frequency may be too low for a two-week pilot.
A text certificate can introduce a new prompt-attack surface and therefore requires irrelevant and contradictory certificate controls.

mechanicalReasons: VLADriveBench already combines observational metrics, selfsplice, semantic CoT interventions, and open-/closed-loop action response.
The candidate adds no new action consequence or decision mechanism.
Activation or interchange intervention is mature causal-interpretability machinery and CVAA already reports silent and amplified VLA pathways.
The requested scope explicitly prohibits activation patching as the contribution.
X-MIND, GeoWorldAD, Latent-CoT-Drive, HybridDriveVLA, and VisualThink-VLA occupy visual and latent thought interfaces.
A swap-only audit is a generic faithfulness probe and the direct checkpoints are not all publicly executable.
Counterfactual VLA and C-CoT directly implement self-reflective or counterfactual action revision.
Same-model critique is not independent repair evidence and can degrade reasoning without external feedback.
Cognitive Dual-Process Planning already routes complex scenes and reports accuracy, routing, and average latency.
The candidate does not price dangerous misses or deadline timeouts.
DualDriveVLA directly invokes the VLM from a trajectory-scorer confidence threshold.
Its public lightweight checkpoint path was not verified, and changing the confidence estimator does not create novelty.
DAST, adaptive continuation, AnytimeReasoner, and HybridDriveVLA already allocate or expand reasoning compute.
More tokens or samples without an action-specific allocation mechanism violates the explicit no-more-compute-only rule.
LinkVLA, SimLingo, CoT4AD, and the cognitive dual-process validator directly cover language-action consistency mechanisms.
Consistency can be jointly wrong and does not identify causal action consequences.
AgentThink exposes tool-CoT reasoning evaluation but no lightweight matched action-head path in the pinned repository.
The executed public demo smoke is tool-level only and cannot close the action hypothesis.
CogDriver directly contributes temporally grounded narratives, sparse temporal memory, coherence distillation, and closed-loop gains.
No distinct causal estimand remains.
DriveTeach-VLA directly trains action-guided visual prompts and vision distillation.
Attention alignment without controlled action consequence is not a new mediation result.
Self-Refine, Reflexion, Counterfactual VLA, and compute-matched reasoning studies cover the method family.
Same-model voting supplies neither an independent repair witness nor a mechanism beyond additional compute.

conclusion.summary: Generic faithfulness probing, activation patching, self-reflection, complexity or confidence routing, consistency training, temporal narratives, and more-compute strategies are directly occupied or explicitly prohibited. Three narrower candidates survive because they introduce an action-level estimand plus a decision mechanism: bounding harmful reasoning influence while preserving useful mediation, pricing slow thought under deadlines and fallback, and requiring an independent certificate for action repair.
dominantEliminationReasons: VLADriveBench already establishes the driving-specific CoT intervention protocol and observational-versus-causal divergence.
Counterfactual VLA, C-CoT, Cognitive Dual-Process Planning, DualDriveVLA, LinkVLA, CogDriver, DriveTeach-VLA, and visual world-action models directly occupy generic method formulations.
General CoT faithfulness, causal mediation, self-correction, and adaptive-compute papers make activation patches, same-model reflection, and extra tokens insufficient contributions.
Several official assets expose papers or repositories but not a pinned lightweight checkpoint, data, and task-level path; full CARLA is not accepted as the initial two-week dependency.

executionEvidence.passedEntry: AgentThink public demo leading-object coordinate ran through the pinned geometry mapping: (-0.06, 6.58)m -> (100, 113) -> pixel center (0.25, 6.75)m, with valid flags true.
executionEvidence.evidenceBoundary: This is a real public-sample tool smoke only. No 7B reasoning model, action head, trajectory evaluation, or CARLA environment was executed, and the smoke was not used as scientific support for a candidate.
